materials.title: Simple Past — finished actions (recap)
contentText:
Use the Simple Past to talk about things that are finished and over — yesterday, last week, this morning.

Regular verbs: add -ed to the base form.
Six irregular forms to know: go → went, have → had, do → did, eat → ate, see → saw, be → was/were.

Important German difference: In German you often use two words for the past (Ich habe gegessen). In English you use ONE word (I ate). Do NOT add "have" when telling a story about the past.
I ate breakfast. (English Simple Past — one word, no have)
They did their homework after school.

materials.title: Tom and Lisa's Tuesday — a conversation
contentText:
Tom: Hey Lisa! How was your Tuesday?
Lisa: Pretty good! I woke up at half past six. Then I had breakfast with my mum.

Tom: What did you eat?
Lisa: I ate toast and a banana. What about you?

Tom: I got up late — at seven. I only had a glass of milk.
Lisa: Oh! Did you go to school by bus?

Tom: Yes, I took the bus. It was cold in the morning. Did you walk?
Lisa: Yes, I walked. It was OK.

Tom: What did you do at lunchtime?
Lisa: I ate a sandwich in the canteen. And you?

Tom: I went home for lunch. My dad made soup.
Lisa: Nice! And after school?

Tom: I did my homework first. Then I watched TV for an hour.
Lisa: I went to football practice. We played really well!

Tom: Cool! And in the evening?
Lisa: I read a book and went to bed at nine.

Tom: I went to bed at half past nine. I was really tired.

materials.title: Tom and Lisa — Simple Past gap-fill
contentText: Tom ___ up late on Tuesday. He only had a glass of milk.
Lisa ___ toast and a banana for breakfast.
Tom ___ the bus to school because it was cold.
At lunchtime, Tom ___ home and his dad made soup.
After school, Lisa ___ to football practice.
Tom ___ really tired in the evening.

materials.title: Tom and Lisa — reading comprehension
contentText: What did Tom eat for breakfast?
How did Lisa travel to school?
What did Tom do after school?
He did his homework and watched TV
They went to bed at the same time

materials.title: Simple Past — spot the mistake
contentText: Yesterday went Lisa to football practice.
Yesterday Lisa went to football practice.
Last week I have watched a good film.
Last week I watched a good film.
Lisa did not went to bed late.
Lisa did not go to bed late.
